title: Expressivity of IQP Feature-Map Quantum Kernels via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
authors: Valeria Repetto, Stefano Melchionna, Romina D'Aurizio
abstract: Quantum kernels are among the most promising methods in quantum machine learning, providing a natural way to embed data into high-dimensional Hilbert spaces via quantum circuits and capturing non-linear relationships in data. Their learning behaviour is governed by the function class they represent, which is formally characterized by the structure of the associated Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS). However, a theoretical characterization of this function class, and of how it depends on the choice of feature map and its hyperparameters, is still lacking. In this work, we focus on the Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial (IQP) feature map and derive a Fourier representation of the associated RKHS generators as finite sums of trigonometric functions evaluated on polynomially transformed input variables, with a finite set of accessible frequencies determined by the circuit construction and scaled by the bandwidth hyperparameter. This representation identifies three bandwidth regimes with qualitatively distinct expressive properties from localised, through multimodal, to periodic. Numerical experiments on synthetic datasets with controlled periodic and multimodal structure, across data dimensions and feature-map configurations, reproduce the three regimes in both supervised classification and unsupervised anomaly detection, benchmarked against a classical Gaussian kernel. These results make the relationship between expressivity and data structure explicit for IQP kernels: expressive power translates into a practical benefit only when the accessible frequencies match with the structure of the data, which provides a criterion for selecting the bandwidth when the periodic or multimodal structure of data is known.
summary: This work theoretically characterizes the expressive power of Quantum Kernels built using the IQP feature map by deriving a Fourier representation of the associated Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space. It demonstrates that the kernel's behavior falls into three distinct regimes—local, multimodal, and periodic—depending critically on the bandwidth hyperparameter. This establishes a crucial criterion: the quantum kernel's power is maximized only when its accessible frequencies match the intrinsic structure of the data.
main_problem: The paper addresses the lack of a theoretical characterization for the function class (expressivity) represented by Quantum Kernels, specifically those derived from the Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial (IQP) feature map.
main_result: The RKHS generators for IQP kernels are shown to have an explicit Fourier sum representation, revealing three distinct bandwidth regimes (localized, multimodal, periodic) that dictate the kernel's expressive power.
method: The authors derived the Fourier representation of the RKHS generators and conducted numerical experiments on synthetic datasets to map the kernel's performance to the data's inherent structure.
model_or_system: The model involves Quantum Kernels (QKs) utilizing the IQP feature map, which maps classical data into a high-dimensional Hilbert space via a unitary transformation. The analysis focuses on how the bandwidth hyperparameter tunes the resulting kernel structure.
key_observables: Test-set F1-score (for classification/anomaly detection), and the structure of the RKHS generators (Fourier sums).
important_parameters: Bandwidth hyperparameter ($b$), number of repetitions ($r$), multimodality ($C$), and dimensionality ($D$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to synthetic datasets with controlled periodic or multimodal structures, and the theoretical characterization is specific to the IQP feature map.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the RKHS generators vs. bandwidth for $D=2$, and supplementary figures show the Test-set F1-score for periodic and multimodal tasks as a function of bandwidth or frequency.
paper_structure: The paper first derives the explicit Fourier sum representation for the IQP kernel's RKHS generators. It then analyzes how the bandwidth parameter induces three distinct expressive regimes (local, multimodal, periodic). Finally, it validates these theoretical findings through numerical experiments on synthetic datasets.
why_interesting: While focused on ML, the explicit connection between the kernel's spectral properties (accessible frequencies) and the underlying data structure provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding how quantum feature maps encode information, which has parallels in analyzing spectral properties in quantum many-body systems.

Each plot displays the values of the kernel k(x, c) where c is fixed at the centre of the square and x = (x1, x2) where x1 and x2 are Cartesian coordinates in the horizontal plane. The periodic-like nature of the kernel becomes visible for larger values of b. It can also be observed that for intermediate values of b the kernel is multi-modal which suggests that it can be used to capture multi-modality or long range interactions in the data. Increasing the number of repetitions increases the complexity of the RKHS generator.
